rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.3 — Why provenance is constitutional ... Without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText. That destroys the ability to answer: Why should I trust this?
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues without provenance, Knowledge becomes indistinguishable from GeneratedText, destroying trust justification.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.7 — Why authority is constitutional ... Without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision. And AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth. That is unacceptable.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues without authority, Recommendation can silently become Decision and AgentOutput can silently become OrganizationalTruth.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.11 — Why epistemic status matters ... 'The service probably owns this database' versus 'The Architecture Board decided that this service owns this database.' The textual similarity may be high. Their epistemic status is radically different.
rationale_evidence.statement: Illustrates why epistemic status matters via a textually-similar but epistemically-radically-different sentence pair.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.15 — Why time is constitutional ... An architecture decision from 2024 may not represent the current architecture in 2026. Therefore HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth.
rationale_evidence.statement: Argues HistoricalTruth≠CurrentTruth, illustrated by a 2024 decision potentially not representing 2026's current architecture.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.27 — Are seven invariants really necessary? Could Provenance be absorbed into Traceability? Not completely. Traceability asks how are objects connected. Provenance asks where did this object come from. They are related but distinct.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Provenance can be absorbed into Traceability, concluding they are related but distinct (connection vs origin).

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.28 — Could authority be part of provenance? Partially. A decision may have AuthoritativeSource. But authority is a governance relationship: Actor-authorizedBy->Decision. Therefore it deserves separate treatment.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Authority can fold into Provenance, concluding authority is a distinct governance relationship deserving separate treatment.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.29 — Could temporal validity be part of provenance? Again, partially. Provenance answers when was this created. Validity asks when is this considered applicable. CreatedAt≠Validity. Keep it separate.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Temporal validity can fold into Provenance, concluding CreatedAt≠Validity requires separate treatment.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.30 — Could epistemic status be part of provenance? No. A source can be known while the statement remains Inference. Provenance≠EpistemicStatus.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Epistemic status can fold into Provenance, concluding Provenance≠EpistemicStatus since a known source does not resolve inference-vs-fact status.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.31 — Could deterministic verification be part of evidence? Yes conceptually. But it deserves explicit treatment because KnowledgeOS has a specific architectural goal: AIReasoning→DeterministicAssurance. Therefore retain it as a constitutional principle.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Deterministic verification can fold into Evidence, retaining it separately due to the specific AIReasoning->DeterministicAssurance architectural goal.

rationale_evidence.anchor: 120.32 — Could feedback be part of traceability? No. Traceability can be completely static: Decision→Commit. Feedback requires Reality→Knowledge. Different property.
rationale_evidence.statement: Tests whether Feedback can fold into Traceability, concluding they are different properties (static connection vs reality-driven update).
